mappings.note: the surds cancel inside 4ac to leave D = -56; a nature-of-roots verdict only, with no roots asked for
the equation must first be expanded out of its bracketed form before D = 0 is imposed, and k = 0 is rejected as non-quadratic; the discriminant is still the operative condition
two demands: decide the nature from D, then STATE the roots, which the key does via -b/2a -- the degenerate quadratic formula; unlike the pure nature items it does not stop at the verdict
the roots are written as a and 6a and pushed through both -b/a and c/a; a ratio-of-roots condition, so the zeroes-coefficients relation rather than the discriminant
expanding the shifted form collapses the constant, leaving x(x-7) = 0; solved entirely by factorisation
a worded number problem translated into x(15-x) = 50, then split; both roots are admissible here since they are the two numbers themselves, which distinguishes it from the reject-a-root word problems
factorises to get the zeroes, then rebuilds a new equation from the sum and product of their squares; the zeroes-coefficients relation is used in both directions
the cleared equation 3x^2 - 6x + 2 = 0 does not factorise and the key applies the formula, giving surd roots; LO-4 rather than LO-3
the rational equation reduces to x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0, which splits cleanly; the difficulty is the algebraic clearing, not the solving method

reduces to 11x^2 + 121x + 218 = 0, which does not factorise, so the formula gives approximate irrational roots; almost certainly a corrupted sign in the stem (defect reported) but coded on the equation as printed
three rational terms combined into 5x^2 + 19x - 30 = 0 and then factorised; heavy manipulation but a factorisation finish
multiplying through by the common denominator gives 2x^2 + 5x + 3 = 0, split into linear factors; one root coincides with an excluded value, which the key does not flag
the middle coefficient is printed as the sum of two reciprocal expressions whose product is 1, so the split is handed over; a pure grouping item with symbolic coefficients
a common factor cancels across the three linear denominators before the quadratic even appears; the residual x(x-4) = 0 is factorisation
the formula is applied and its discriminant recognised as the perfect square (2a+1)^2; LO-4 because the route is the formula, even though the key adds a factorised check
symbolic coefficients in b where the discriminant reduces to the constant 81; only the formula makes that collapse visible, so LO-4
clearing the two fractions gives x^2 + x - 2 = 0, split into (x+2)(x-1); factorisation after rearrangement

explicitly demands COMPLETING THE SQUARE, which the frame has no outcome for; LO-4 is the nearest since the quadratic formula is that method generalised and the roots (-1 +/- sqrt(33))/4 do not factorise (gap reported)
the formula with the discriminant collapsing to 36b^2; the same symbolic-coefficient family as the 4x^2 - 4a^2x item, honestly one outcome
the near-twin of the (x+4)(x+7) item but with a minus sign that makes the quadratic factorise into (x-1)(x-2); the contrast is exactly factorisation versus the formula
solved by grouping the four printed terms rather than splitting a middle term; still the factorisation outcome, with no formula and no discriminant
reduces an identity to the perfect square (xb-ya)^2 = 0 and reads off the consequence; no quadratic equation is actually solved and no discriminant used, so the fit is weak -- flagged as a poor fit
the formula with a discriminant simplifying to (p^2+q^2)^2; the surd disappears only after that recognition, which is LO-4's characteristic move
the constant 2a^2+5ab+2b^2 must itself be factorised before the middle term can be split; a two-level factorisation, the hardest LO-3 item in the chapter
equal roots is the hypothesis, so D = 0 is imposed and collapses to (ad-bc)^2 = 0; a discriminant proof, distinct from the factorisation proofs above
